chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Al-Nawfali, from Al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), from his forefathers (peace be upon him), who said:

The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Whoever comforts one who is grieving, will be clothed in a garment of honor in the Standing (Place of Reckoning) with which he will be beautified.'

key_terms.الْمَوْقِفِ: the Standing (referring to the Place of Reckoning on the Day of Judgment)
key_terms.حُلَّةً: a garment of honor or splendid dress

ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual reward for comforting someone who is grieving according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In al-Kafi, Shaykh al-Kulayni records this chain from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) to emphasize that comforting the grieving is a profound act of worship that yields tangible spiritual rewards. The 'garment of honor' (hullah) symbolizes divine acceptance and elevated status in the Hereafter, reflecting the Shia emphasis on social empathy as a path to spiritual purification. This tradition underscores the communal responsibility to alleviate sorrow, linking interpersonal kindness directly to eschatological glory.
